On-demand: Webinar on robustness in pig genetics

Pigs that are strong enough to deal with a challenge – and pigs that manage to overcome an infection relatively easily: that is the thought behind having robust and resilient pigs in swine production. A recent webinar delved deeper into this concept. It is available for watching on demand for free.

Vincent ter BeekEditor of Pig Progress / Topic: Pigs around the world

Oct 9

News

The line-up of the webinar, from left to right: Robert Hoste, Wageningen Social & Economic Research; Laurent Roger, Axiom; Vincent ter Beek, Pig Progress; and Enea Labescau, Axiom.

The webinar, which was broadcast on 29 September, was recorded in cooperation with pig genetics company Axiom. The webinar featured 3 expert speakers.

Click here to view the webinarA glimpse of pig production in the future

Robert Hoste is senior pig production economist at Wageningen Social & Economic Research. He kicked off the webinar with a glance into the future of pig production on the basis of production data.

He discussed various locations where pig production of the future is going to take place and he mentioned 7 different factors determining that: the human factor; technology; production efficiency; feed availability; animal health; production costs and risk stability. ‘Where will future pig production take place?’ Hoste concluded. ‘I would put my money on South America, but it’s not only where it will take place but also which elements need to be fulfilled to be competitive in the future.’

Balancing performance and robustness

Next on stage was Enea Labescau, member of the genetics team at Axiom. She zoomed in on what is happening in the fattening period, and emphasised that the breeding company does not select solely for maximum growth rate, and does not go for an optimisation of feed efficiency without considering overall robustness. Rather, she said, the aim is to balance performance and robustness during the selection strategy and continuously monitor health and functional traits.

She concluded, with regard to robustness, that the company’s goal is not to breed the best animals in perfect environments, but the most resilient and reliable animals in real farming conditions.

Robustness and immunity in every step

The message of robustness also echoed in Laurent Roger’s presentation. Roger is technical and marketing director at Axiom. In an overview slide, from farrowing to fattening, he showed how robustness and immunity traits are built into every step of pig production.

With regard to maternal quality, he pointed to various automated Precision Livestock Farming (PLF) tools that help the company get there, for instance the development of cameras capable of detecting the sow’s position; the development of a behaviour analysis algorithm; or the use of sound to characterise behaviour.

translationZh:
足够强壮以应对挑战的猪——以及能够相对轻松地克服感染的猪：这就是在养猪生产中拥有稳健且具有抗逆性的猪背后的理念。最近一场网络研讨会深入探讨了这一概念。该研讨会现可免费点播回看。

该网络研讨会于9月29日播出，是与猪遗传育种公司Axiom合作录制的。研讨会共有3位专家演讲嘉宾。

**展望未来养猪生产**

Robert Hoste是瓦赫宁根社会与经济研究中心的资深养猪生产经济学家。他以生产数据为基础，展望了未来养猪生产的前景，拉开了研讨会的序幕。

他讨论了未来养猪生产将发生的各个地区，并提到了决定这一点的7个不同因素：人为因素、技术、生产效率、饲料可获得性、动物健康、生产成本和风险稳定性。“未来的养猪生产将在哪里进行？”Hoste总结道。“我会把赌注押在南美洲，但问题不仅在于在哪里进行，还在于需要满足哪些要素才能在未来具有竞争力。”

**平衡生产性能与稳健性**

接下来登场的是Enea Labescau，Axiom遗传学团队成员。她聚焦于育肥阶段的情况，并强调该公司不仅仅为最大生长速度进行选育，也不会在不考虑整体稳健性的情况下追求饲料效率的优化。相反，她说，目标是在选育策略中平衡生产性能与稳健性，并持续监测健康和功能性状。

她就稳健性总结道，公司的目标不是在完美环境中培育最好的动物，而是在真实养殖条件下培育最具抗逆性和可靠性的动物。

**每一步都融入稳健性与免疫力**

稳健性的理念也贯穿了Laurent Roger的演讲。Roger是Axiom的技术与营销总监。在一张从分娩到育肥的概览幻灯片中，他展示了稳健性和免疫性状如何被融入到养猪生产的每一个环节。

在母体品质方面，他指出了多种自动化精准畜牧（PLF）工具，帮助公司实现这一目标，例如开发能够检测母猪位置的摄像头；开发行为分析算法；或利用声音来表征行为。
